findings.title: Cancel near-due reminders without waiting for the cron
findings.body: Scheduled reminders are now only marked cancelled, leaving SendGrid cancellation to the 15-minute cron. If a booking is cancelled just after a cron run and its reminder is due 12 minutes later, SendGrid sends the reminder before the next run. That run then deletes the now-past reminder row before processing cancellations. Near-due reminders need synchronous cancellation; otherwise cancelled bookings still receive reminders even when the cron runs reliably.

findings.title: Rescheduling bypasses the deferred cancellation fix
findings.body: Passing true makes deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancel immediately even when the original reminder is scheduled days away. Those cancellations occupy SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation slots until their original send dates, recreating the quota exhaustion described in this PR. Once the quota is full, the helper only logs the failure and never marks the reminder cancelled, so the cron cannot retry it and the old reminder is sent. Rescheduling needs a durable deferred cancellation path too.

findings.title: Handle cancellation failures per reminder
findings.body: The try/catch surrounds the entire cancellation loop, so one rejected SendGrid request skips every remaining reminder and also skips Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete). Because Prisma queries are lazy, even the database deletions queued for earlier successful cancellations never execute. A persistently failing batch can therefore block other cancellations across cron runs until reminders are sent or removed as past. Catch failures per reminder and execute each successful cancellation's deletion independently.

findings.title: Await reminder cancellation persistence before completing the request
findings.body: The asynchronous cancellation helpers are called from forEach without awaiting or collecting their promises, and they are absent from the subsequent Promise.all. These helpers now perform the only database update or deletion that prevents the cron from sending a cancelled booking's reminders. The handler can return while those writes are pending; in a serverless deployment, execution may be suspended before they finish, leaving live reminders behind despite a successful cancellation response. Include these promises in the awaited work.
